risks: Assessment is static and based on supplied source and reported fixtures; hashes, infrastructure behavior and numerical results were not independently executed or verified.

The 8192 MiB memory and 1800-second wall-time budgets are not established by a representative training benchmark. Budget exhaustion must terminate this single attempt without automatic retry or protocol adjustment.

One initialization and a repeatedly explored training-only evaluation cohort support descriptive discovery only. Any strictly positive Macro-F1 delta is a point result, not independent confirmation or population-level evidence.

The simplex control has different update magnitude, nonsmooth max-scale derivatives and computational cost. Winning against it would not uniquely establish a benefit from noncommutativity; trained pinching and alignment controls are outside this diagnostic.
Checkpoint replay verifies only the first evaluation batch. This satisfies the frozen contract but does not certify full-evaluation reload parity or independent metric recomputation.

Reported parent fixtures replace scientific computation and admission guards. They support failure/publication handling, not training correctness, resource feasibility or scheduler-wide descendant cleanup.
theory_mapping: The full condition implements the analytic initial-effect logarithm, centered utility operator, smooth Frobenius normalization and differentiable matrix exponential without detaching the utility-to-measurement path or adding a second epsilon.
The simplex implementation is algebraically equivalent to the specified bounded utility tilt: centering the exponent subtracts a classwise constant that cancels during normalization.

All three conditions copy the same FP32-initialized, FP64-cast native state, retain 81028 parameters and use identical predetermined sample orders and optimizer settings. Four epochs times ceil(3124/32) gives 392 steps per condition and 1176 total.

Training gradients use fit labels only; evaluation occurs after the fourth epoch without checkpoint selection. This tests joint optimization of the new computational graph, rather than repeating the stopped fixed-checkpoint intervention.

The Gibbs argument supports own-class aggregate improvement at fixed states and utilities, not task-loss improvement during training. The harmful-CE witness and lack of established novelty remain applicable.
Positive-39 Macro-F1 is implemented consistently. Primary positivity is retained independently of CE and simplex comparisons, while formal promotion and L5 acceptance remain excluded.

Source-bound admission, idle-only paired configuration updates, one-attempt/no-replay settings, checkpoint hashing and reload checks, and publication only after successful child completion are consistent with the bounded lifecycle contract.
